modules.title: Talking About the Past
modules.description: Describe completed events in sequence.
modules.content:
## Learning goal
Describe completed events in sequence.

## Key rule
Use the simple past for finished actions. Regular verbs often end in -ed; irregular verbs have special forms.

## Example
I visited my cousin yesterday and watched a film.

## Practice
Read the example aloud. Change one detail to make it true for you, then write two original sentences. Check the grammar, tone and context.

## Reminder
Clear and accurate English is more useful than complicated wording.

vocabulary.meaning: move something to a later time
knowledge gained by doing or seeing something

Integrate precise vocabulary, argument, tone and structure.

Adapt register to audience, make claims proportionate to evidence and revise for clarity.

Clear and accurate English is more useful than complicated wording.

modules.description: Recognise English letters, spell simple words and practise common letter sounds.
modules.content: English uses 26 letters. The letters have uppercase forms (A, B, C) and lowercase forms (a, b, c). Vowels are A, E, I, O and U. The other letters are consonants. modules.description: Use basic subject pronouns to talk about yourself and other people.
modules.content: A pronoun replaces a noun or a person's name. The subject pronouns are I, you, he, she, it, we and they. Use 'I' for yourself, 'you' for the person you speak to, 'he' for a male person, and 'she' for a female person. Use 'it' for a thing or animal when its sex is not specified.
